productionControlConfig.closedCandleHandling: only just-closed 15m candle; source timestamp is candle closeTime

selectionPolicy: Finite preregistered registry; all candidates and failed results are retained. Selection uses nested inner-fold stability, never peak single-fold NetR.

registry.hypothesis: A compressed range followed by a volume-confirmed breakout and a shallow retest can preserve continuation edge without late chasing.
registry.marketMechanism: Order-flow imbalance from a range expansion is tested when former resistance becomes support.
registry.expectedRegime: BULL with BTC/ETH agreement and non-extreme breadth
registry.entryLogic: Prior-bar clean high breakout, current-bar retest of the former high, close back above the level, controlled extension.
registry.invalidationLogic: Retest closes below former resistance or stop is hit before target.
registry.expectedFailureMode: Failed breakout, thin volume, or entry after an already extended impulse.

registry.hypothesis: A stricter breakout volume threshold should separate clean continuation from noisy range breaks.
registry.marketMechanism: High participation confirms a state change before the support retest.
registry.entryLogic: Thirty-bar level break, high relative volume, shallow retest and reclaim without extension above one ATR.
registry.invalidationLogic: Level rejection or a wide retest that signals distribution.
registry.expectedFailureMode: Volume spike without follow-through or broad market disagreement.

registry.hypothesis: A longer compression and a conservative retest can reduce false breakouts even at the cost of fewer trades.
registry.marketMechanism: Energy accumulation in a narrow range creates asymmetric continuation only after the level is defended.
registry.entryLogic: Twenty-bar break after compression, retest within one ATR, positive momentum re-acceleration.
registry.invalidationLogic: Retest fails or the signal is too far from EMA/level.
registry.expectedFailureMode: Compression resolves in the opposite direction or lacks breadth support.

registry.hypothesis: A mature higher-timeframe uptrend should reward controlled pullbacks that re-accelerate from EMA/structure.
registry.marketMechanism: Continuation buyers defend a known value area after weak counter-trend supply is absorbed.
registry.entryLogic: Bull trend age, one-to-four ATR pullback, close above EMA with positive momentum acceleration.
registry.invalidationLogic: Trend alignment breaks or the pullback exceeds the structural risk band.
registry.expectedFailureMode: Trend exhaustion and a deeper regime transition masked as a pullback.

registry.hypothesis: Shallower pullbacks with a stronger momentum turn may avoid buying exhausted rebounds.
registry.marketMechanism: Fast re-acceleration after a shallow reset indicates demand remains dominant.
registry.entryLogic: Short controlled pullback, RSI recovery, volume expansion and limited EMA distance.
registry.invalidationLogic: No momentum turn or close under the fast EMA.

registry.hypothesis: Longer trend age and a deeper but still bounded pullback may improve entry location when volatility is elevated.
registry.marketMechanism: A deeper liquidity sweep that holds structure can reset extension without invalidating the trend.
registry.expectedRegime: BULL with elevated but non-spiking volatility
registry.entryLogic: Deeper pullback, structure hold, bullish close and no late chase.
registry.invalidationLogic: Structure breaks or price remains below EMA after the pullback.
registry.expectedFailureMode: Trend age becomes exhaustion rather than continuation.

registry.hypothesis: A measured volatility expansion from compression can create directional continuation before the move becomes crowded.
registry.marketMechanism: Volatility re-pricing plus volume participation produces a temporary directional imbalance.
registry.entryLogic: Compression, range expansion, volume confirmation, close near high and controlled extension.
registry.invalidationLogic: Expansion lacks follow-through or is an isolated spike.

registry.hypothesis: A stricter compression and expansion threshold should reject single-bar anomalies.
registry.marketMechanism: Sustained range expansion with two-sided confirmation is more likely to represent information arrival.
registry.entryLogic: Tight compression, current and prior expansion confirmation, high volume and positive benchmark alignment.
registry.invalidationLogic: One-bar spike, weak close, or extension beyond one ATR.
registry.expectedFailureMode: Breakout occurs after the exploitable move has already happened.

registry.hypothesis: A lower threshold variant tests whether the structural idea survives realistic signal sparsity without a narrow optimum.
registry.marketMechanism: Early but confirmed expansion may retain more of the move than late breakout entry.
registry.entryLogic: Compression followed by positive expansion, moderate participation and no extreme extension.
registry.invalidationLogic: Expansion fails to hold the compression boundary.
registry.expectedFailureMode: False positive expansion in a range.

registry.hypothesis: A support breakdown followed by a controlled retest from below can provide cleaner short entries than late trend rejection.
registry.marketMechanism: Former support becomes overhead supply after trapped longs exit on the retest.
registry.entryLogic: Prior-bar clean support breakdown, retest of former support, bearish close and controlled downside extension.
registry.invalidationLogic: Retest reclaims support or the stop is hit before target.
registry.expectedFailureMode: Breakdown is absorbed and becomes a bear trap.

registry.hypothesis: Higher-volume, longer-lookback breakdowns may reduce noise while preserving a retest edge.
registry.marketMechanism: A broad support failure attracts trend followers and offers a defined invalidation on the retest.
registry.entryLogic: Thirty-bar support break, strong volume, shallow retest and rejection.
registry.invalidationLogic: Reclaim of support or a retest wider than the defined ATR distance.

registry.hypothesis: A compression-to-breakdown variant tests whether a prepared support failure is more stable than an impulsive drop.
registry.marketMechanism: Compression releases downside and the retest exposes stranded demand at the old floor.
registry.entryLogic: Compressed support break, bounded retest and downside re-acceleration.

registry.hypothesis: A failed upside breakout with reclaim failure can expose trapped breakout buyers and create a distinct reversal edge.
registry.marketMechanism: Failed expansion leaves late longs positioned above invalidation while downside confirmation accelerates exits.
registry.entryLogic: Recent upside break, loss of breakout level, failed reclaim, bearish confirmation and no late downside chase.
registry.expectedFailureMode: Breakout resumes after a shallow shakeout.

registry.hypothesis: Requiring a stronger failed reclaim should reduce false reversals at the expense of sample size.
registry.marketMechanism: Repeated inability to hold the breakout level creates asymmetric downside once trapped demand capitulates.
registry.entryLogic: High-volume upside break, two-bar failure, failed reclaim and momentum turn below the level.
registry.expectedFailureMode: The market is trending and the failed breakout is only a pause.

registry.hypothesis: A lower-volume rejection variant tests whether failed structure, rather than volume alone, carries the reversal signal.
registry.marketMechanism: The key information is inability to hold the breakout, not the absolute size of participation.
registry.entryLogic: Upside probe, close below the level, lower high, bearish candle and bounded extension.
registry.invalidationLogic: Higher-high reclaim or lack of downside confirmation.

registry.hypothesis: A mature higher-timeframe downtrend should reward controlled rebounds that reject resistance and re-accelerate lower.
registry.marketMechanism: Counter-trend supply is absorbed at value/resistance before continuation sellers regain control.
registry.entryLogic: Bear trend age, one-to-four ATR rebound, close below EMA and negative momentum acceleration.
registry.invalidationLogic: Trend alignment breaks or rebound exceeds the structural risk band.
registry.expectedFailureMode: Downtrend is ending and rebound becomes a reversal.

registry.hypothesis: Shallow rebounds with a stronger downside turn may avoid shorting an exhausted decline.
registry.marketMechanism: Fast resumption after a shallow reset indicates supply remains dominant.
registry.entryLogic: Short bounded rebound, RSI rejection, volume expansion and limited EMA distance.
registry.invalidationLogic: No downside momentum turn or close above the fast EMA.
registry.expectedFailureMode: Low-liquidity drift or a bear-market bounce.

registry.hypothesis: A deeper bounded rebound can improve short entry location during elevated volatility while preserving a downtrend structure.
registry.marketMechanism: Liquidity is collected above the recent low before sellers reassert control.
registry.expectedRegime: BEAR with elevated but non-spiking volatility
registry.entryLogic: Deeper rebound, resistance hold, bearish close and no late downside chase.
registry.invalidationLogic: Resistance breaks or price remains above EMA after the rebound.
registry.expectedFailureMode: Trend age becomes exhaustion rather than continuation.
